title: fusion.catalog/v2
description: The role catalog, catalog/catalog.json, copied unchanged into the Prior bundle as catalog.json. One entry per canonical role; every Prior role id (Prior modules/fusion/profiles.json at 167c605) and every Claude agent name (agents/*.md) appears exactly once across the entries, through claude_name, prior_ids or an alias. One entry per function a user starts, each a Claude agent or a skill (Prior hand-over H1). v2 adds entries beside an unchanged roles (decision 261023-1854-does-the-catalog-gain-entries-under-fusion-catalog-v1-or-as-v2.md, option 2): the version name says the shape to the two decoders that read exact key sets, Prior's (internal/fusionhost/external_catalog.go decodes schema and roles with DisallowUnknownFields and an exact key count, and gains entries at its step 28 on request 76) and the module's (adapters/prior/fusionmodule/internal/steps/catalog.go LoadCatalog), so no further key is admitted here either. Support states: only prior supported is executable on Prior; planned ships for inspection and refuses dispatch, aliases included; unsupported refuses dispatch and needs no profile (Prior answer 67.2). Rules JSON Schema cannot check and the catalog tests (plan step 5) enforce: canonical ids are unique across entries (jq -r '.roles[].id' | sort | uniq -d prints nothing); claude_name values are unique; every prior_ids entry that differs from the canonical id is listed in aliases with its domain; no alias id equals a canonical id or another alias; every role whose prior state is not unsupported has catalog/profiles/<id>/profile.json, and the bundle carries profiles/<id>.json and profiles/<id>.md for it. Entry rules the catalog tests enforce (catalog/src/render.ts checkCatalogDocument and checkEntries, and the shared table catalog/testdata/catalog-decode-cases.v2.json the Go decoder runs too): entry ids are unique; an entry has kind agent exactly when agents/<id>.md exists and kind skill exactly when skills/<id>/SKILL.md exists; class is one of asks, dispatches, plain; requires holds each of host.question.v1, host.exec.v1, host.dispatch.v1 at most once and nothing else; every argument kind is one of Prior's five; an entry whose prior state is supported names a profile with at least one prior part, and the entry services those prior parts name are exactly its requires. A profile named by an agent entry and by its role is one profile.

claude_name.description: The Claude Code agent name, agents/<claude_name>.md; null for a role with no Claude agent.

prior_ids.description: Every Prior role id this entry covers; empty for a role Prior has never named. An id other than the canonical one is an alias and must appear in aliases.

aliases.description: New-binding aliases of the canonical role, each carrying the domain the binding preserves (Prior answer 67.3: code-reviewer and data-reviewer alias reviewer with domains code and ontology).

support.description: One state per host, never an absent key.

entry_service.description: The host services an entry may require beyond what its workflow declares: the three Prior binds as model tools of a role run (internal/supervisor/general_tools.go).

entry.description: One function a user starts. The key set is fusion's proposal in request 76, held to the same exactness as a role.

id.description: The Claude agent name (agents/<id>.md) or the skill directory name (skills/<id>/SKILL.md).

profile.description: The profile directory under catalog/profiles/: the role id for an agent, skill-<id> for a skill. Needed on disk only once the entry's prior state is not unsupported.

class.description: Prior's class rule C1, narrow: asks puts a question to the user, dispatches starts another agent, plain does neither.

support.description: One state per host, never an absent key.

arguments.description: The argument declaration Prior's admission reads (internal/fusionhost/admission.go; inventory.schema.json arguments).

name.description: The flag or option as typed, a positional's name, a parameter line's **<Keyword>:**, or the first message's name.

values.description: The closed set of accepted values, when there is one.
